data.narrative:
Ocius Technology, a Series B defense and security company, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 10 peers (2 public, 8 private) operating in the same sector and stage. The peer set includes Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Castelion ($1.0B), and Defense Unicorns ($1.0B), alongside public comparables DRSHF and IDEAFORGE.NS.

Two triangulation methods are applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the company's $176M total raised (proxied as base value) and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $334M. Peer-median benchmarking across the seven same-sector, same-stage private comparables produces a $1.0B implied valuation, with the peer set ranging from $300M floor to $3.0B ceiling. These methods produce a weighted triangulated range of $284M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $667M.

The analysis supports a valuation band centered around $667M, though meaningful dispersion exists. The gap between stage-progression ($334M) and peer-median ($1.0B) reflects material uncertainty around whether Ocius's competitive positioning and the $176M Program of Record contract justify positioning at or above median peer value. Key sensitivities include contract execution risk, differentiation relative to Dream Security and Harmattan AI, and whether the public comparables' multiples remain representative of private market conditions.
